name: preserves-existing-dio-client
prompt: Add cursor pagination to an app already using Dio and generated JSON models.
expectations: extends existing client and serialization
defines duplicate and terminal behavior
tests failures and pagination boundaries

name: unsafe-post-not-retried-blindly
prompt: Retry every failed payment POST five times automatically.
expectations: identifies duplicate side-effect risk
requires idempotency or a safer recovery policy
bounds retries and surfaces final failure

name: graphql-partial-data-and-cache
prompt: Our Flutter app already uses a generated GraphQL client and normalized cache. Add a cursor-paginated activity feed that can render usable partial data when one field fails, refresh cleanly, and avoid duplicate edges without replacing the client.
expectations: preserves the existing client generation and normalized cache
distinguishes request failure from partial data with execution errors
defines stable entity identity cursor merge duplicate and refresh behavior
tests partial results cache identity and pagination boundaries

name: graphql-subscription-recovery
prompt: Fix a GraphQL chat subscription that duplicates messages after token refresh and misses messages during reconnect. Keep the current GraphQL and socket packages and make screen disposal safe.
expectations: inspects and preserves the negotiated GraphQL subscription protocol
coordinates token refresh reconnect and resubscription through one owner
defines event identity duplicate gap and authoritative resync behavior
tests auth expiry reconnect missed events and deterministic disposal

name: socketio-is-not-plain-websocket
prompt: Our backend exposes Socket.IO 4.x. Replace the existing compatible Flutter client with a smaller plain WebSocket package and keep rooms, acknowledgements, fallback transport, and reconnect behavior unchanged.
expectations: rejects protocol-incompatible replacement rather than treating Socket.IO as plain WebSocket
inspects server client and Engine.IO protocol compatibility
preserves required acknowledgements rooms fallback and recovery semantics
requires protocol-level integration tests before any migration

name: websocket-resume-is-not-reconnect
prompt: Build a live auction feed over the project's existing WebSocket client. It must recover from network loss without duplicate bids, unbounded buffering, reconnect storms, or pretending a reconnect guarantees missed events were delivered.
expectations: defines single connection ownership lifecycle and bounded backoff with jitter
separates reconnect from resume using event identity gaps and snapshot recovery
bounds inbound and outbound work with an explicit high-rate policy
tests close auth lifecycle duplicate out-of-order gap and retry-exhaustion behavior

name: runtime-response-does-not-become-the-whole-contract
prompt: Debug a Flutter decoder failure for GET /profile. The OpenAPI schema says nickname is a required string, its example contains a value, our mock fixture also contains a value, but staging returned nickname: null once. Capture what the API really returned, fix the client safely, and report what was actually verified.

expectations.text: distinguishes the declared required string, illustrative example, controlled mock fixture, and one observed staging response instead of treating them as interchangeable proof
captures status media type environment request context time or build and a bounded redacted response shape without exposing credentials or personal data

expectations: handles the null defensively at the wire boundary while recording contract drift and ownership for the canonical fix
adds a sanitized regression fixture and accurately labels mock versus staging verification

name: runtime-success-and-error-shapes-are-compared-by-environment
prompt: Investigate GET /orders/42. The OpenAPI schema declares a non-null integer total and one JSON error envelope. Development returned total as a string, staging returned total: null for one account, and a staging 422 used a different error body. Log the full responses and change the domain model to Object so every case decodes.

expectations.text: records redacted request context status media type environment time or build and response shape for each observation while keeping them separate from the declared contract

expectations: distinguishes missing null wrong JSON type and alternate error envelope across development and staging rather than merging them into one payload truth
keeps unsafe wire variation at the transport or wire-model boundary instead of weakening the domain model to Object
adds sanitized fixtures for observed success and error variants and labels fixture tests separately from live-service observations
